import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 786

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)
-/

open Filter Real

open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos786

open Erdos786

-- TODO : add variants that allow repetition.
-- According to the updated website, Erdos likely intended repetitions to be allowed here
-- however, the analogous questions without repetition are also open.
/--
`Nat.IsMulCardSet A` means that `A` is a set of natural numbers that
satisfies the property that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$
can only hold when $r = s$.
-/
def Set.IsMulCardSet {α : Type*} [CommMonoid α] (A : Set α) :=
  ∀ (a b : Finset α) (_ :↑a ⊆ A) (_ : ↑b ⊆ A) (_ : a.prod id = b.prod id),
    a.card = b.card

/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of density $> 1 - \epsilon$
such that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_786.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ A.IsMulCardSet := by
  sorry

/--
Is there some set $A\subset\{1, ..., N\}$ of size $\geq (1 - o(1))N$ such that
$a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_786.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (A : ℕ → Set ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (_ : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)),
    ∀ N, A N ⊆ Set.Icc 1 (N + 1) ∧ (1 - f N) * N ≤ (A N).ncard ∧ (A N).IsMulCardSet := by
  sorry

/--
An example of such a set with density $\frac 1 4$ is given by the integers $\equiv 2\pmod{4}$
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_786.parts.i.example (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A = { n | n % 4 = 2 }) :
    A.HasDensity (1 / 4) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet := by
  subst hA
  constructor
  · -- Exactly `(n + 1) / 4` of the naturals below `n` are `≡ 2 (mod 4)`.
    have hfin : ∀ n : ℕ, ((Finset.range n).filter fun m ↦ m % 4 = 2).card = (n + 1) / 4 := by
      intro n
      induction n with
      | zero => simp
      | succ n ih =>
        rw [Finset.range_add_one, Finset.filter_insert]
        split
        · rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simp)]; omega
        · omega
    have hcard : ∀ n : ℕ, ({m : ℕ | m % 4 = 2} ∩ Set.Iio n).ncard = (n + 1) / 4 := by
      intro n
      have hset : {m : ℕ | m % 4 = 2} ∩ Set.Iio n
          = ↑((Finset.range n).filter fun m ↦ m % 4 = 2) := by
        ext m; simp [Set.mem_Iio, and_comm]
      rw [hset, Set.ncard_coe_finset, hfin]
    rw [Set.HasDensity]
    have hpd : ∀ n : ℕ, ({m : ℕ | m % 4 = 2}).partialDensity Set.univ n
        = (((n + 1) / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) := by
      intro n
      rw [Set.partialDensity, Set.inter_univ, Set.univ_inter, hcard, Nat.ncard_Iio]
    simp only [hpd]
    -- Squeeze `⌊(n + 1) / 4⌋ / n` between `1 / 4 - 1 / n` and `1 / 4 + 1 / n`.
    have hbdd : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
        1 / 4 - 1 / (n : ℝ) ≤ (((n + 1) / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ∧
          (((n + 1) / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 4 + 1 / (n : ℝ) := by
      intro n hn
      have hn0 : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
      have h1 : 4 * ((n + 1) / 4) ≤ n + 1 := by omega
      have h2 : n + 1 < 4 * ((n + 1) / 4) + 4 := by omega
      have c1 : (4 : ℝ) * (((n + 1) / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) + 1 := by exact_mod_cast h1
      have c2 : (n : ℝ) + 1 < 4 * (((n + 1) / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 4 := by exact_mod_cast h2
      constructor
      · rw [le_div_iff₀ hn0]; field_simp; linarith
      · rw [div_le_iff₀ hn0]; field_simp; linarith
    have hlim : ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ 1 / 4 + c * (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 4)) := by
      intro c
      simpa using Tendsto.const_add (1 / 4 : ℝ)
        (Tendsto.const_mul c tendsto_one_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat)
    refine tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'
      (by simpa using hlim (-1)) (by simpa using hlim 1)
      (eventually_atTop.2 ⟨1, fun n hn ↦ ?_⟩) (eventually_atTop.2 ⟨1, fun n hn ↦ ?_⟩)
    · simpa using (hbdd n hn).1
    · simpa using (hbdd n hn).2
  · -- Every element of the set is exactly divisible by `2`, so the `2`-adic valuation of a
    -- product of distinct such elements is the number of factors.
    have key : ∀ s : Finset ℕ, ↑s ⊆ {n : ℕ | n % 4 = 2} →
        (s.prod id).factorization 2 = s.card := by
      intro s hs
      have hmem : ∀ i ∈ s, i % 4 = 2 := fun i hi ↦ hs hi
      have h0 : ∀ i ∈ s, id i ≠ 0 := fun i hi ↦ by
        have := hmem i hi; simp only [id]; omega
      rw [Nat.factorization_prod h0]
      simp only [Finsupp.finsetSum_apply]
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (g := fun _ ↦ 1) fun i hi ↦ ?_, Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul,
        mul_one]
      have h4 := hmem i hi
      have hi0 : i ≠ 0 := by omega
      have hd1 : 2 ^ 1 ∣ i := by omega
      have hd2 : ¬ (2 ^ 2 ∣ i) := by omega
      rw [Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization Nat.prime_two hi0] at hd1
      rw [Nat.Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization Nat.prime_two hi0] at hd2
      simp only [id]
      omega
    intro a b ha hb hprod
    rw [← key a ha, ← key b hb, hprod]

/--
`consecutivePrimesFrom p k` gives the set of `k + 1` consecutive primes that are at least `p` in
size. If `p` is prime then this is the set of `k + 1` consecutive primes `p, p_1, ..., p_k`-/
noncomputable def consecutivePrimesFrom (p : ℕ) (k : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
    (Finset.range (k + 1)).image (Nat.nth (fun q ↦ q.Prime ∧ p ≤ q))

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem nth_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    Nat.nth (fun q ↦ q.Prime ∧ p ≤ q) 0 = p := by
  simpa [Nat.nth_zero] using IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by
    aesop (add simp [IsLeast, mem_lowerBounds])

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma consecutivePrimesFrom_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : consecutivePrimesFrom p 0 = {p} := by
  simpa [consecutivePrimesFrom] using nth_zero hp

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma consecutivePrimesFrom_two_one : consecutivePrimesFrom 2 1 = {2, 3} := by
  have h : Nat.nth (fun q ↦ q.Prime ∧ 2 ≤ q) 1 = 3 := by
    exact Nat.nth_count (p := (fun q ↦ q.Prime ∧ 2 ≤ q)) (by decide : (3).Prime ∧ 2 ≤ 3)
  ext q
  simp only [consecutivePrimesFrom, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_insert,
    Finset.mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hq⟩
    cases i with
    | zero => simpa [← hq] using .inl (nth_zero Nat.prime_two)
    | succ i => grind
  · rintro (rfl | rfl); exact ⟨0, by grind, nth_zero Nat.prime_two⟩; exact ⟨1, by grind⟩

-- Reworded slightly using https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-14.pdf p. 81
-- See https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-02.pdf p. 182 for the multiplicity one condition
/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then, for a sufficiently large prime `p`, take the sequence of
consecutive primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_k$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{p_i} < 1 < \sum_{i=1}^{k + 1} \frac{1}{p_i},
$$
and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $\frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / rexp 1) :
    ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in atTop, p.Prime → ∃ k,
      ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (1 : ℝ) / q < 1 ∧
        1 < ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p (k + 1), (1 : ℝ) / q ∧
          letI A := { n | ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (n : ℕ).factorization q = 1 }
          A.HasDensity (1 / rexp 1 - ε) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet := by
  sorry

end Erdos786

findings.description: The conclusion `A.HasDensity (1 / rexp 1 - ε)` requires an exact density, whereas Selfridge's construction provides a density greater than this bound. Here `A` is fixed by the `let`, so one cannot repair the equality by thinning A. In fact, the full universally quantified assertion is inconsistent: put c = 1/e and apply it with ε = c/2 and ε = c/3 at a prime beyond both eventual thresholds. The reciprocal-sum crossing conditions determine a unique k, so the same A would have the two distinct densities c/2 and 2c/3. I proved the negation of the full assertion in `/workspace/review/selfridge.lean`, independently of all sorry-dependent declarations.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Some applications of graph theory to number theory,” p. 81, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-14.pdf: “Selfridge showed that to every ε there is a sequence of density > 1/e − ε satisfying (12),” followed by the prime-block construction used in this declaration.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the final conjunction by `(∃ δ : ℝ, 1 / rexp 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet`. Update the docstring to say density greater than 1/e − ε, rather than exactly equal to it.

reformulations.difference: Lean restricts the question to 0 < ε ≤ 1, whereas the source asks for every ε > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The unrestricted version implies the restricted one immediately. Conversely, for ε > 1, reuse the witness at ε = 1: its density δ satisfies δ > 0 > 1 − ε, and all other conditions are unchanged. The equivalence is proved in `/workspace/review/reformulations.lean` as `Review786.epsilon_restriction_iff`.

reformulations.difference: Lean places A N inside {1,…,N+1}, rather than {1,…,N}, while keeping the size lower bound normalized by N.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given Lean's witnesses, take B N = A N \ {N+1}. The multiplicative-cardinality property is hereditary, and removing this endpoint loses at most one element. Replacing f N by f N + 1/N preserves little-o(1) and gives the required size bound for N > 0; N = 0 is harmless. The converse follows by interval inclusion. This equivalence is proved in `/workspace/review/reformulations.lean` as `Review786.interval_shift_iff`.

review.notes: The Finset definition intentionally selects the distinct-factor variants. The archived source explicitly recognizes these variants as still open; the negative results discussed there concern repetition-allowed products and should not be transferred to these declarations. The currently downloaded linked database also records problem 786 as open. Direct access to the live problem page was Cloudflare-blocked, so live-page changes after the archive date could not be checked. All declarations and relevant default/boundary cases were reviewed. The refutation, equivalences, and boundary tests compile without errors or warnings in `/workspace/review/{selfridge,reformulations,boundaries}.lean`; the certified results have no `sorryAx` dependency.

demonstrated.claim: The declaration's exact type is false: two admissible ε values force the same uniquely determined prime block to have different exact densities.

submission.summary: /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean negates the original declaration's type using type_of%, without invoking its proof. The file compiles without errors or warnings, and the disproof depends only on standard logical axioms, not sorryAx.

import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«786»
/-! The cited Selfridge construction gives a density lower bound, not an exact density. -/

open Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Review786

-- Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge: false, since two admissible ε values force
-- the same uniquely determined prime block to have two different exact densities.
theorem selfridge_false : ¬ (type_of% @Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge) := by
  intro h
  let c : ℝ := 1 / Real.exp 1
  have hc : 0 < c := by dsimp [c]; positivity
  have h₁ := h (c / 2) (by change 0 < c / 2 ∧ c / 2 < c; constructor <;> linarith)
  have h₂ := h (c / 3) (by change 0 < c / 3 ∧ c / 3 < c; constructor <;> linarith)
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 (h₁.and h₂)
  obtain ⟨p, hpN, hp⟩ := Nat.exists_infinite_primes N
  obtain ⟨k, hk₀, hk₁, hDk, _⟩ := (hN p hpN).1 hp
  obtain ⟨l, hl₀, hl₁, hDl, _⟩ := (hN p hpN).2 hp
  -- Nonnegative summands make the crossing index unique.
  have hm : Monotone (fun k ↦
      ∑ q ∈ Erdos786.consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (1 : ℝ) / q) := by
    intro i j hij
    apply Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
    · exact Finset.image_subset_image (Finset.range_mono (by omega))
    · intros; positivity
  have hkl : k = l := by
    rcases lt_trichotomy k l with hlt | heq | hlt
    · linarith [hm (show k + 1 ≤ l by omega)]
    · exact heq
    · linarith [hm (show l + 1 ≤ k by omega)]
  subst l
  have hd := tendsto_nhds_unique hDk hDl
  change c - c / 2 = c - c / 3 at hd
  linarith

#print axioms selfridge_false
end Review786

submission.summary: Replaced the exact-density requirement with the existence of a density δ > 1/e − ε, and updated the docstring accordingly. Only these two lines were changed. The file compiles with no errors and only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

  · rintro ⟨i, hi, hq⟩
    cases i with
    | zero => simpa [← hq] using .inl (nth_zero Nat.prime_two)
    | succ i => grind
  · rintro (rfl | rfl); exact ⟨0, by grind, nth_zero Nat.prime_two⟩; exact ⟨1, by grind⟩

-- Reworded slightly using https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-14.pdf p. 81
-- See https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-02.pdf p. 182 for the multiplicity one condition
/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then, for a sufficiently large prime `p`, take the sequence of
consecutive primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_k$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{p_i} < 1 < \sum_{i=1}^{k + 1} \frac{1}{p_i},
$$
and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $> \frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / rexp 1) :
    ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in atTop, p.Prime → ∃ k,
      ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (1 : ℝ) / q < 1 ∧
        1 < ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p (k + 1), (1 : ℝ) / q ∧
          letI A := { n | ∑ q ∈ consecutivePrimesFrom p k, (n : ℕ).factorization q = 1 }
          (∃ δ : ℝ, 1 / rexp 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ) ∧ A.IsMulCardSet := by
  sorry

end Erdos786
